# Exterior receiving theorem: collision endpoints and marked-label parity

Status: self-contained proposed mathematical derivation plus finite exact diagnostics. The determinant, Pfaffian, fixed/free-endpoint and exterior-representation algebra is classical. Historical novelty of the quantitative receiving composition is UNKNOWN. No external theorem audit or physical workload validation occurred.

## 1. Models, conventions and outputs

Vertices are ordered `0,...,n-1`. For an undirected weighted graph let

\[
 L_{xx}=d_x=\sum_y r_{xy},\qquad L_{xy}=-r_{xy}\quad(x\ne y),
 \qquad K(t)=e^{-tL}.
\]

Rates are fixed, nonnegative, symmetric and independent of the state. Set `1 <= k <= n` and `X=(x_1<...<x_k)`. Distinguish three outputs:

1. **Collision model.** Identical independent walkers start at X. Stop at their first simultaneous occupation of one vertex. The endpoint is the sorted occupied set, with an additional cemetery outcome for prior collision. On a path, sorted positions also identify each initial walker because order cannot change before collision. On a cycle they do not identify the cyclic rotation of labels or winding.
2. **Conditional collision endpoint.** The complete sorted endpoint, or its number of sites in a supplied bin B, conditional on no collision before t. A certified positive survival lower bound is required for a certified relative/conditional error.
3. **Interchange parity.** In the original interchange process, select the labels initially at X. If their final sites in that label order are `(sigma(x_1),...,sigma(x_k))`, let `s_X(sigma)` be the sign of the permutation sorting that sequence. This is a binary endpoint observable on every graph. It is not their full joint endpoint law.

An optional nonnegative site potential `v_x` replaces L by `L+diag(v)`. In the collision model this means independent deaths at the corresponding site hazards. Equivalently its surviving endpoint weights include

\[
 \exp\{-\int_0^t\sum_{i=1}^k v_{X_i(u)}\,du\}.
\]

Thus nonnegative potentials also supply exact Laplace transforms of total exposure until collision. Death and collision share a cemetery outcome unless a richer output is separately constructed. All finite-bit executions below use integer rates, integer potentials and t=1. # Consequential exterior extension: a certified receiving and sampling operation

The strongest completed extension here is a **direct finite-bit receiver for the complete sorted endpoint of k identical walkers, conditional on no collision**, on weighted paths and cycles. It uses one-particle heat rows and fixed/free-endpoint Pfaffians of order at most 2k. It visits O(k log n) mass queries and never enumerates the binomial endpoint space or rejects a full trajectory until rare survival occurs.

A second operation applies to the **original interchange process on arbitrary graphs**: compute and certify the endpoint order parity of k selected labels, including branching graphs. This is a genuine nonlocal binary endpoint observable, but the underlying exterior/hook sector is classical. It does not give the full correlated labelled/color endpoint distribution.

The receiving composition is reviewable and implemented below. Historical novelty, external correctness, useful physical application and superiority over an equally informed classical heat/Pfaffian incumbent are **UNKNOWN**. The package is an extension of the supplied finite-bit workflow, not a claimed mathematical or technological breakthrough.

## Exact receiving contract

Input: supplied nonnegative state-independent symmetric rates on an ordered path or cycle, k distinct starting sites, a horizon, and one-particle row approximations with certified l1 errors epsilon_i. For the executed integer implementation the horizon is 1. Let

\[
 \delta=\sum_{i=1}^k\epsilon_i,\qquad
 s_0>0\text{ a certified survival lower bound},\qquad
 D=k\lceil\log_2 n\rceil.
\]

The receiving theorem proves:

- Whole living endpoint measure l1 error <= delta, even when approximate minors are signed.
- Whole one-bin endpoint-count coefficient vector l1 error <= delta.
- Direct conditional count sampling TV <= delta/s0 plus bounded-fair-bit rejection error.
- Direct conditional complete sorted-endpoint sampling TV <= `D(delta/s0+2^-A)` for A rejection attempts at each binary decision.

All mass queries must be exact marginals of the same approximate heat-row matrix. Each next endpoint is chosen by binary search, using prefix/suffix masses from a block Pfaffian. Clipping signed child masses is included in the proof; it is not an uncharged numerical repair.

# Primary-literature confrontation

Read/search date: 2026-10-16. These are primary publications or their authors' original-paper copies. Only bibliographic links and short paraphrases are retained here; no third-party full text or executable is bundled. This bounded review cannot establish priority for the receiving composition.

## Direct determinant and Pfaffian incumbents

- **Karlin and McGregor, “Coincidence probabilities,” Pacific Journal of Mathematics 9 (1959), 1141–1164.** [Publisher original](https://msp.org/pjm/1959/9-4/pjm-v9-n4-p13-p.pdf). The introduction and its birth-and-death noncoincidence statement identify the k-particle killed transition determinant. The discussion on printed pp. 1143–1144 identifies odd-particle cyclic-order positivity. Therefore neither all-k path determinants nor the odd-cycle observation can be claimed here as new. The supplied exterior report's link ending `p12-s.pdf` should not be used as the bibliographic identity for this separate paper: the directly inspected publication is the p13 paper above.

- **N. G. de Bruijn, “On some multiple integrals involving determinants,” Journal of the Indian Mathematical Society 19 (1955), 133–151.** [Author's institutional original-paper copy](https://pure.tue.nl/ws/files/1920642/597510.pdf), [institutional metadata](https://research.tue.nl/en/publications/on-some-multiple-integrals-involving-determinants/). Its introduction explicitly treats one determinant integrated over an ordered measure space, includes sums, and distinguishes even/odd Pfaffian forms. The finite ordered-set identity used here is a specialization, not an invention. Site terminal weights, including polynomial count fugacities, enter the same determinant columns.

- **John R. Stembridge, “Nonintersecting paths, Pfaffians, and plane partitions,” Advances in Mathematics 83 (1990), 96–131.** [Original-paper copy](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~kratt/bedlewo/stemb-nonint.pdf), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/0001-8708(90)90070-4). Theorem 3.1 on printed pp. 106–107 handles free terminal regions, and Theorem 3.2 on pp. 108–109 handles some fixed and some free endpoints, including a phantom vertex for parity. This directly covers the structural mass-query algebra used by the conditional endpoint receiver.
